title: Photo 203 · 콜로설 · 팔레흐 · 무릎 꿇기 옆 (양 무릎) · 남아시아 40대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult South Asian woman in her late 40s, faint lines at the eyes and mouth, rich warm brown skin tone with golden undertones, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, a wide round afro with a gold headband, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears heavy chandelier earrings and has squared-off coffin nails.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so deep from front to back that her belly reaches beyond one edge of the frame and her rear beyond the other. A giantess built on a completely even scale, every part of her enlarged by the same amount: massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full bust, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs and thick heavy calves, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body, her shoulders span more than four head-widths, each hand is as wide as a normal woman's torso and each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. No single part stands out more than another, no hanging folds, not pregnant, her whole body scaled up together into one immense smooth silhouette that towers over the viewer. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The flesh is softer and looser at this age, each fold hanging lower and settling further over the one below it. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it drops, settles and presses down onto the thighs beneath it.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, a coarser surface grain, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, crepey texture in the deepest folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Russian Palekh miniature style — a deep black ground with fine gold linework and small jewel-toned scenes of firebirds, horses and winter forests in crimson, emerald and ultramarine, a gold border band following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs, gold filigree filling the space between every band. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Kneeling upright on the platform seen from directly to her side, both calves folded beneath her thighs and her rear settled back onto her heels, her back straight, her near hand resting on her thigh and her far arm held back so nothing crosses in front of her torso, her head turned toward the camera, the whole depth of her body read from the side, full body head to knees filling the frame.

Footwear: Extreme gold peep-toe platform stiletto pumps, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the gold filigree glinting, the black ground reading clearly as paint on skin rather than as fabric, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide.
